newsitem.title: USA: AT&T names Somers CFO; sets long-distance hike.
newsitem.headline: AT&T names Somers CFO; sets long-distance hike.

text.p: AT&T Corp. said Wednesday it named senior Bell Canada executive Daniel Somers as chief financial officer and senior executive vice president of the telecomunications giant.
At the same time, the company said it would boost prices effective May 1 on business long-distance services to offset payments to payphone owners required under a plan established by U.S. regulators.
Somers, succeeds Richard Miller, who left the company in March amid a management restructuring.
Somers will direct financial strategy and organisation for AT&T, and report to Robert Allen, AT&T's chairman and chief executive, and be part of the chairman's office.
Somers, whose new assignment will take effect in mid-May, is the current Chairman and Chief Executive of Bell Cablemedia Plc, an affiliate of BCE Inc.'s Bell Canada.
"Dan's broad skills and accomplishments make him ideally suited for the CFO role at this pivotal point in AT&T's history," Allen said.
Under the rate hike, AT&T said it would increase prices for interstate toll-free services by 7 percent and prices for business international and interstate outbound services by 2 percent.
The Federal Communications Commission plan requires long-distance carriers to compensate payphone owners for coinless calls -- typically calling card and toll-free calls.

On April 15, local telephone companies were to begin billing AT&T and other long-distance companies for the 1.8 million payphones operated by the local companies. AT&T's share of the new costs is $26.21 per phone per month, it said.

In passing the costs along to customers, AT&T said it continued to believe that the payphone increases were unjustifiably high. It pledged to roll back the price increases if it succeeds in efforts to cut the payments to payphone owners.
AT&T, other long-distance carriers and state regulators have appealed the FCC order. The case is scheduled to be heard in mid-May by the Court of Appeals in Washington, it said.
